title: Trump ‘not concerned’ about WPS tensions: It ‘would be taken care of’

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — United States President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he is “not concerned” about tensions in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) as it “would be taken care of.”
Trump made the remark when asked how concerned he was about tensions in the WPS and whether he was ready in case the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) was invoked.

“I am not concerned at all, I am not concerned about that at all, that would be taken care of,” Trump said in response to reporters during a bilateral meeting with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in Malacañang.

Filipino pundits have floated the possible invocation of the MDT in response to aggressive actions by China in the West Philippine Sea during Marcos’ term. These incidents have so far resulted in a serious injury to a Philippine Navy personnel member and the deaths of two Chinese sailors.
The MDT between Manila and Washington calls on each country to defend the other in the event of an armed attack.

Articles IV and V of the MDT state that an armed attack in the Pacific, including anywhere in the South China Sea, against either country’s public vessels, aircraft or armed forces, including their coast guards, would trigger their mutual defense commitments.
However, the treaty does not clearly define the term “armed attack.”

Questions about what constitutes an armed attack under the MDT arise whenever Beijing conducts activities that Manila considers escalatory, such as using military-grade lasers and water cannons or ramming ships.
So far, the Philippine side has said that such acts by China do not yet constitute an armed attack.
In 2024, Marcos said the MDT would be invoked once a Filipino serviceman dies as a result of an attack by a foreign power.
During Trump’s visit, Marcos also cited the 75-year military alliance between Manila and Washington under the MDT, which was signed on Aug. 30, 1951.
“The United States is our only treaty ally, and our relationship has continued to grow and evolve over the many years,” Marcos said.
In a related development, Trump said he was working with Marcos to expand defense cooperation between Manila and Washington.
According to Trump, he has approved $5 billion worth of arms sales to the Philippines since taking office.
He also noted that the United States is building 21 new weapons manufacturing plants to expand the capacity of its military-industrial base.
“So you won’t have to wait so long when you order,” Trump told Marcos.
“Nobody makes weapons like we do, and we’re making it much faster,” Trump continued. “We have everything there is to have. Everybody wants it, and we only deal with friends.” /mcm/dl
